maya_capacity: Heads up — I'm updating throughput model for Spring HackWeek (Apr 7-9) + DST drift. Expect morning spikes 07:00-10:00 local regions. Need quick sanity check on headroom numbers :chart_with_upwards_trend:
juan_infra: Copied. What's baseline numbers you're using?
maya_capacity: Baseline (global steady): ~2.1M tokens/sec, ~9k concurrent inference requests. Model mix heavy: 60% chat (context 1k tokens), 30% completions, 10% embeddings.
juan_infra: OK — threw together quick scenarios:```
scenario,multiplier,tokens_sec,conc_req,est_gpu_hours_delta
normal,1.0,2100000,9000,0
hackweek_morning,1.75,3675000,15750,14000
hackweek_peak,2.2,4620000,19800,26000
```
kevin_sre: What's baseline p99 / tail we use in the model? If we hit 2.2x, what's our buffer? Can't exceed 200ms P50 target.
maya_capacity: Baseline p50=75ms, p95~210ms during controlled peak tests. With 2.2x we simulated p95~480ms; p99 >1s. So headroom is thin unless we change routing/batching.
sophie_dev: Could we push more aggressive batching or increase max_batch_size? That helps tokens/sec but will likely increase tail latencies. Trade-off depends on SLOs.
juan_infra: Options: pre-warm a small dedicated GPU pool in eu-west-1 for morning window, or route ~30% non-critical traffic to a smaller quantized variant (int8) to reduce pressure.
alyssa_finance: Quick question — rough delta on cost for pre-warm vs fallback routing? We have ~$200k headroom this quarter.
juan_infra: Back-of-envelope: pre-warm reserve adds ~14k GPU hours over the month -> roughly $95k/month. Fallback routing (int8) on 30% of traffic reduces compute spend on those requests by ~35% (~$60k savings projected). Net if we pre-warm + fallback = ~+$35k projected. Need exact calc but that's the magnitude.
ops-bot: node-drain: gpu-node-42 drained today during canary patch test — removed 4 GPUs temporarily. No customer impact observed. :white_check_mark:
kevin_sre: Recommendation: set autoscale min_capacity +20% for hackweek morning windows, reduce cooldown to 2m, enable burst_buckets sized for 15m windows. Also schedule a focused stress test Wed 06:30 UTC to validate p95/p99.
maya_capacity: I'll push updated model with those autoscale policies and a canary schedule. Can someone run the stress test and capture p99/p95 traces? @kevin_sre @juan_infra
kevin_sre: On it. I'll also run network egress checks — last time EU->US fallback added ~120ms extra for cross-region fallbacks.
juan_infra: I'll prepare fallback routing config and spin up a tiny quantized variant in staging. Will attach perf profiles. Tagging this for a postmortem comparison with last year's hackweek.
alyssa_finance: If we exceed budget threshold we'll trigger emergency throttle plan (pause non-customer background jobs). Not ideal but ready as a safety valve.
maya_capacity: :thumbsup: Plan looks good. I'll update the forecast doc and send to product + ops. Will ping #all-hands tomorrow with a short summary and the recommended mitigations.
